source.title: Frequency Principle: Fourier Analysis Sheds Light on Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: Zhi-Qin John Xu; Yaoyu Zhang; Tao Luo; Yan Xiao; Zheng Ma

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Reports natural-label train and test accuracy and relates Fourier properties to generalization, but does not test the original random-label memorization comparison or the interventions in the other versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports frequency-convergence results on MNIST, CIFAR10, and a parity task. Those results concern frequency fitting, not a behavior named by V1–V8, so they are not rows for those versions; the frequency/generalization relation is recorded under fits_no_version. Cited findings from other papers are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study tests frequency-dependent learning and offers a spectral explanation of generalization. Natural-label accuracy alone does not test V1's coexistence of random-label memorization and natural-label generalization under matched architectures and recipes. Parity is not a random-label comparison. No results test the interventions or relationships in V2–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors propose that a low-frequency learning bias helps explain good generalization on MNIST/CIFAR10 and poor generalization on parity. Their generalization explanation draws on spectral comparisons; their theoretical results establish frequency priorities under idealized assumptions.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments analyze Fourier components during training and their relation to generalization; they do not reproduce the random-label memorization procedure or the interventions in the mapped versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports frequency-fitting behavior across architectures, losses, optimizers, and datasets; the reported natural-label accuracy rows use MNIST and CIFAR10 with different architectures and batch sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: Natural-label MNIST and CIFAR10 test accuracies are 0.963 and 0.72, respectively; the study does not measure random-label memorization in these models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: These particular networks generalize above chance on natural-label image classification.

fits_no_version.finding: Projection and filtering analyses show lower response frequencies converging faster than higher frequencies across several architectures, losses and datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient-trained neural networks often learn lower response frequencies before higher ones.

fits_no_version.finding: Along examined directions, natural-image targets concentrate at low response frequencies and trained outputs recover dominant components; parity outputs depart from the target spectrum.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Alignment between neural networks' low-frequency bias and target frequency structure may help explain differences in generalization.

record.problems: Natural-label train/test accuracy is reported for only two image datasets in the mapped version; the paper does not test random-label memorization or the train/test gap under matched natural-label and random-label conditions. The frequency analyses examine selected directions or coarse-grained filtered components, not the full high-dimensional spectrum.
record.rows_left_out: Frequency-convergence outcomes in Figures 1–4 and Fourier comparisons in Figure 5 are discussed under fits_no_version because they do not measure a behavior named by V1–V8. The parity result is qualitative and does not report a numerical generalization measure.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and chance held-out accuracy, together with natural-label generalization using the same architectures and training recipes.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Matched convolutional versus fully connected generalization comparisons and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under specified tuning budgets and recovery interventions.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out error across data sizes, dropout strengths and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps and comparisons with other complexity measures.
Test accuracy after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Different architectures, optimizers and batch sizes appear in the experiments, but their presence does not constitute controlled tests of V3–V5. References to sharpness and other generalization measures report related work rather than this study's measurements.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy at chance; Inception, AlexNet, and MLP random-label comparisons; ImageNet.

rows.subject: tanh-DNN (784-400-200-10)
rows.operation_detail: Trained on MNIST with cross-entropy loss and Adam; reports training and test accuracy.
rows.note: Natural-label held-out accuracy is reported; no random-label comparison is made.
rows.check: The reported MNIST training accuracy of 0.951 and test accuracy of 0.963 are correct, but there is no matched random-label experiment establishing V1's coexistence claim.

rows.subject: ReLU-CNN (two convolutional layers followed by fully connected DNN)
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR10 with cross-entropy loss and Adam; reports training and test accuracy.
rows.note: Natural-label held-out accuracy is reported; no random-label comparison is made.
rows.check: The reported CIFAR10 training accuracy of 0.98 and test accuracy of 0.72 are correct, but there is no matched random-label experiment establishing V1's coexistence claim.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
